si_refractive_index_li1980.model: n^2 = eps(T) + (L(T)/lam^2)*(A0 + A1*T + A2*T^2); eps = e0 + e1*T + e2*T^2 + e3*T^3; L = exp(-3*dLL); dLL = c0 + c1*T + c2*T^2 + c3*T^3 (lam in um, T in K)

coefficients.note_c0: printed as -0.071; must be read as -0.071 % (-7.1e-4) to reproduce Li's Table 1 (derived check)

si_refractive_index_li1980.valid_range: 1.2-14 um; 100-750 K recommended (L branches cover 20-1600 K)
si_refractive_index_li1980.source: H. H. Li, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 9, 561 (1980), eq. (22), Table 1

si_refractive_index_frey2006.model: n^2 - 1 = sum_{i=1..3} S_i(T) lam^2/(lam^2 - lam_i(T)^2); S_i, lam_i = 4th-order polynomials in T
si_refractive_index_frey2006.valid_range: 1.1-5.6 um, 20-300 K ONLY (polynomials diverge near 325 K)
si_refractive_index_frey2006.uncertainty: absolute +/-1e-4 (Table 1: 8.67e-5 at 1.5 um, 295 K); fit residual 1e-4
si_refractive_index_frey2006.source: B. J. Frey, D. B. Leviton, T. J. Madison, Proc. SPIE 6273, 62732J (2006), Tables 2, 4, 5 (arXiv:physics/0606168)
si_refractive_index_frey2006.notes: Sellmeier dn/dT at 293 K (1.82e-4) undershoots the paper's own measured Table 4 (1.94e-4 at 1.3 um, 295 K)

si_refractive_index_recommended.uncertainty: +/-5e-4 absolute (derived); Li vs Frey disagree by 4.1e-3 at 1310 nm, 2x Li's stated uncertainty
si_refractive_index_recommended.source: Li 1980 + Frey 2006; Franta et al., Appl. Surf. Sci. 421, 405 (2017) agrees with Frey level (3.50555 at 300 K)

si_dn_dT_1310nm.uncertainty: recommended 1.94e-4 +/-0.07e-4 at 300 K; 2.13e-4 +/-0.1e-4 at 375 K (spread of sources)
si_dn_dT_1310nm.source: Li 1980; cross-checks: Frey 2006 Table 4 = 1.94e-4 (1.3 um, 295 K, printed); Franta 2017 = 1.87e-4 (300 K) / 2.00e-4 (375 K) (read-off+derived); Lukes 1959/60 = 2.04e-4 (1.327 um, 300 K, printed in Li Table A-3); Cocorullo 1999 at 1523 nm = 1.855e-4 (300 K), scaled to 1310 nm = 1.95e-4 (derived); Wang 2025 SOI 224 nm film ~2.3e-4 (298-338 K, derived, noisy)
si_dn_dT_1310nm.notes: Textbook REF.dnSi_dT = 1.86e-4 is the 1523 nm, 300 K value (Cocorullo 1999). Della Corte group (1.5 um) found no dependence on doping type/level/orientation.

si_d2n_dT2_1310nm.uncertainty: sources span 1.7e-7 to 2.8e-7 (Franta 1.88e-7 at 300 K, 1.70e-7 at 375 K; Cocorullo 1523 nm 2.58e-7 at 300 K, 2.35e-7 at 375 K)
si_d2n_dT2_1310nm.source: Li 1980; Franta 2017; Cocorullo, Della Corte, Rendina, APL 74, 3338 (1999)

si_dn_dT_cocorullo_1523nm.source: G. Cocorullo, F. G. Della Corte, I. Rendina, Appl. Phys. Lett. 74, 3338 (1999)

si_group_index_material_1310nm.uncertainty: +/-0.02 [corrected by checker from +/-0.01: Frey 2006 Sellmeier gives 3.689 at 1.31 um, 295 K; Franta 2017 gives 3.690 at 300 K; both ~0.016 above Li]

si_absorption_1310nm.valid_range: 300 K; band edge moves ~27 meV red by 400 K, still < ~0.02 dB/cm at 1260 nm (derived estimate)
si_absorption_1310nm.source: M. A. Green, Sol. Energy Mater. Sol. Cells 92, 1305 (2008)

ring_thermal_shift_ceiling_1310nm.model: dlam/dT <= lam*(dn_Si/dT)/n_g,Si + lam*(neff/ng)*alpha_Si  (all electric energy in Si; first-order perturbation with material dispersion)
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling_1310nm.valid_range: any Si-core, SiO2-clad ring at 1260-1360 nm, 273-400 K
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling_1310nm.uncertainty: -2 to -4 pm/K with Franta dn/dT; +3 pm/K with Lukes at 300 K
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling_1310nm.source: this file, from Li 1980 and Okada & Tokumaru 1984
ring_thermal_shift_ceiling_1310nm.notes: In GHz/K: 12.4 (300 K), 13.6 (375 K), 13.9 (400 K). Lightmatter M4B.3 prints '~15 GHz/C' (85.8 pm/K) in its introduction; that is 1.08-1.26x above this ceiling over 273-400 K and needs dn_Si/dT ~2.35e-4, which Li reaches only near 500 K.

sio2_index_fused_silica.uncertainty: +/-1e-5 vs CHARMS after air correction (derived check)
sio2_index_fused_silica.source: I. H. Malitson, JOSA 55, 1205 (1965); Leviton & Frey arXiv:0805.0091 (1.44845 at 1.2 um, 1.44502 at 1.5 um, 295 K)

sio2_index_films.source: Rodriguez-de Marcos et al., Opt. Mater. Express 6, 3622 (2016); Franta et al., Proc. SPIE 9890, 989014 (2016); Arbabi & Goddard, Opt. Lett. 38, 3878 (2013)

sio2_dn_dT.valid_range: measured 30-310 K (fused silica, 1.2-1.5 um); linear extension above 300 K is assumed
sio2_dn_dT.source: Leviton & Frey arXiv:0805.0091 Table 6 (8.40-8.45e-6 at 295 K); Corning 7980 data sheet 9.6e-6 at 1128.64 nm (polynomial gives 9.53e-6 at 1310 nm, inferred); Arbabi & Goddard 2013 PECVD (0.95+/-0.10)e-5; Elshaari 2016 PECVD (0.96+/-0.09)e-5

si3n4_index_lpcvd.source: K. Luke et al., Opt. Lett. 40, 4823 (2015)

si3n4_dn_dT.source: Arbabi & Goddard, Opt. Lett. 38, 3878 (2013); Elshaari et al., IEEE Photonics J. (2016)

k_si_bulk.uncertainty: +/-5 % (handbook values vary 68.8-157 per Electronics Cooling 1998; Glassbrenner & Slack 1964 ~156 at 300 K is recalled, not re-checked)
k_si_bulk.source: V. Palankovski, PhD thesis TU Wien (2000) sec. 3.2.3; consistent with CRC/TPRC set 168/148/98.9 at 273/300/400 K (quoted from memory, assumed)

k_si_film.valid_range: single-crystal SOI film 150-300 nm, 273-400 K, undoped to ~1e18 cm^-3
k_si_film.uncertainty: +/-15 % (73-95 W/(m K) at 220 nm, 300 K, from the +/-10 W/(m K) of the anchor measurement)
k_si_film.source: anchored to M. S. Aubain & P. Bandaru, MRS Proc. 1267, DD12-01 (2010): 260 nm SOI device layer, 90 +/- 10 W/(m K) at room temperature. Cross-checks: Ju & Goodson, APL 74, 3005 (1999) (up to 50 % reduction for films down to 74 nm; fit under-predicts there: 45 vs ~74); Asheghi et al., J. Heat Transfer 120, 30 (1998) (~40 % below bulk at 0.42 um; fit over-predicts: 105 vs ~89)
k_si_film.notes: Corrected by checker 2026-10-09: previous version used d0 = 250 nm (69 W/(m K) at 220 nm), anchored to '32 and 38 W/mK at 50 and 80 nm' attributed to the Aubain & Bandaru MRS paper, which reports only 260 nm, 90 +/- 10 W/(m K). Heavy doping 1e19-1e20: ~80 % of undoped (Electronics Cooling 1998 estimate, assumed). Asheghi et al., J. Appl. Phys. 91, 5079 (2002) covers 1e17-3e19 doped films.

k_sio2.uncertainty: +/-10 %; PECVD ~10 % below thermal oxide for films > 100 nm; apparent 0.83-1.23 for 50-500 nm PECVD
k_sio2.source: Palankovski 2000; Corning 7980 data sheet; S.-M. Lee & D. G. Cahill, J. Appl. Phys. 81, 2590 (1997); arXiv:1905.08570

k_low_k_ild.source: 2014 microfin/IR thermometry study of SiOC:H and SiC:H films (abstract via search)

k_metals.model: Wiedemann-Franz k = L0*T/rho (+ phonon part for W, TiN)
k_metals.source: handbook bulk values (assumed); W phonon fraction 62 % (arXiv:2505.07613)

thermal_boundary_resistance.uncertainty: Si/SiO2 printed; metal/dielectric ~10x larger (printed ratio, 2008 study), value inferred
thermal_boundary_resistance.source: Lee & Cahill 1997 (equivalent to ~20 nm SiO2); 2008 Cr/PECVD SiO2 study (abstract)
thermal_boundary_resistance.notes: Si/SiO2 is ~1.4 % of a 2 um BOX: negligible. Metal/oxide ~0.25 um oxide equivalent: not negligible for a metal heater <=1 um from the ring.

cp_si.uncertainty: within 0.5 % (298 K) and 1.2 % (400 K) of NIST-JANAF (20.000 and 22.142 J/mol K)

density.source: Si standard value; Corning 7980 data sheet (2.201 g/cm3); film ranges assumed

cte_si.source: Y. Okada, Y. Tokumaru, J. Appl. Phys. 56, 314 (1984)

cte_sio2.valid_range: fused silica; thermal oxide assumed similar

thermo_mechanical_contribution.model: expansion: lam*(neff/ng)*alpha_Si; photoelastic: oxide biaxial stress E/(1-nu)*(alpha_Si-alpha_SiO2) ~0.18 MPa/K times stress-optic 1e-12..4e-12 /Pa
thermo_mechanical_contribution.valid_range: SOI ring on thick Si substrate
thermo_mechanical_contribution.uncertainty: photoelastic part is an order-of-magnitude estimate (<~1 pm/K), no source
thermo_mechanical_contribution.source: derived; E, nu and stress coefficient (35.0 nm/(cm MPa)) printed on Corning 7980 data sheet

plasma_dispersion_nsm2011_1300nm.model: dalpha = a*dNe^b + c*dNh^d ; dn = -(p*dNe^q + r*dNh^s) (dN in cm^-3)
plasma_dispersion_nsm2011_1300nm.source: M. Nedeljkovic, R. Soref, G. Z. Mashanovich, IEEE Photonics J. 3, 1171 (2011); transcribed from flexcompute/tidy3d default_nedeljkovic_soref_mashanovich_coeffs (primary PDF not opened)

plasma_dispersion_soref1987_1300nm.source: R. A. Soref, B. R. Bennett, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 23, 123 (1987)

plasma_dispersion_temperature_dependence.model: Drude: dn ~ N/(n m*_opt); dalpha ~ N/(n m*^2 mu_opt)
plasma_dispersion_temperature_dependence.source: trend from D. M. Riffe, JOSA B 19, 1092 (2002) (effective mass rises with T); magnitudes assumed

fca_cross_sections_1300nm.model: small-signal derivatives of NSM 2011; SB 1987 linear

tpa_beta_1310nm.valid_range: ~1.3 um, 300 K; rises with T (1.55 um: 0.76 at 300 K vs 0.42 at 5.5 K, Sinclair 2019); >300 K not measured (assume +0.1 to +0.3 %/K)
tpa_beta_1310nm.uncertainty: 0.5-2.0 cm/GW: factor-3 disagreement between z-scan groups, not resolved
tpa_beta_1310nm.source: Q. Lin et al., APL 91, 021111 (2007); A. D. Bristow et al., APL 90, 191104 (2007); M. Dinu et al., APL 82, 2954 (2003); G. F. Sinclair et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 11, 044084 (2019)

free_carrier_lifetime.model: SRH (Borghi: tau_n 35 ns, tau_p 22.5 ns, trap E_i+0.10 eV, 1e15 p-type)
free_carrier_lifetime.uncertainty: geometry and surface dependent; reverse-bias value assumed (Turner-Foster 2010 not opened)
free_carrier_lifetime.source: M. Borghi et al., Opt. Express 29, 4363 (2021); D. Dimitropoulos et al., APL 86, 071115 (2005); A. C. Turner-Foster et al., Opt. Express 18, 3582 (2010)

doped_si_resistivity.model: rho = 1/(q N mu); mu from Masetti (300 K) or Arora (250-500 K), full ionization
doped_si_resistivity.valid_range: reference table at 23 C; Arora 250-500 K, 1e13-1e20 (weak above 1e19)
doped_si_resistivity.uncertainty: table values printed; models +/-10 % (Arora -13 % at 1e20 n)
doped_si_resistivity.source: resistivity-dopant table for c-Si at 23 C (via search); G. Masetti et al., IEEE TED 30, 764 (1983); N. D. Arora et al., IEEE TED 29, 292 (1982) (coefficients via nextnano/DESSIS and COMSOL docs)

doped_si_tcr.model: TCR = (1/rho) drho/dT with Arora mobility, full ionization
doped_si_tcr.uncertainty: +/-50 % (incomplete ionization at 1e17-1e18 lowers it; Arora weak above 1e19)
doped_si_tcr.source: derived from Arora 1982; textbook fit for the G25 heater is 1e-3 /K (REF.heaterTcrPerK, derived)

metal_heater_tcr.uncertainty: process dependent; low-stress TiN nonlinear, can change sign; W film sign depends on deposition
metal_heater_tcr.source: AIP Advances 2022 microheater comparison (TiN 487 ppm/C, Pt 2641, Ti 4146); TaN heater patent (TiN ~550 ppm/C); Sensors & Actuators A 2008 (TiN stress); Micromachines 2024 (W films); thick-film W patent (0.0046 /C); Cu, silicides assumed

ge_pd_responsivity_1310nm.model: R = eta*lam[um]/1.23984; assumed constant vs T at 1310 nm (+/-3 % over 0-105 C, assumed)
ge_pd_responsivity_1310nm.uncertainty: T dependence not measured at 1310 nm in sources found
ge_pd_responsivity_1310nm.source: physics; Lightmatter OFC 2025 talk via textbook REF ([LM-T]); L. Colace et al., J. Lightwave Technol. (2008) (defective Ge loses responsivity with T)

ge_pd_dark_current_vs_T.uncertainty: Ea +/-0.03 eV for the x1.6/10 C reading; device dependent. [checker: Balbi et al., Physica E 2009 (same group) report x1.6-1.9 per 10 C, i.e. Ea up to ~0.5 eV and up to ~x65 at 105 C vs 25 C]
ge_pd_dark_current_vs_T.source: L. Colace et al. (2008): x1.6 per 10 C; S. J. Koester et al. (2006): x10 at 85 C vs RT (abstracts); GOI p-i-n study (abstract)

si_bandgap.source: C. D. Thurmond, J. Electrochem. Soc. 122, 1133 (1975) (as reproduced in device texts)

si_intrinsic_density.source: K. Misiakos, D. Tsamakis, J. Appl. Phys. 74, 3293 (1993); alt. R. Couderc et al., J. Appl. Phys. 115, 093705 (2014): ni = 1.541e15*T^1.712*exp(-Eg0/(2kT)) (Eg0 model not read)

pn_builtin_voltage.model: Vbi = (kT/q) ln(NA ND / ni(T)^2), step junction, full ionization, no BGN
pn_builtin_voltage.uncertainty: band-gap narrowing at ~1e18 lowers Vbi by a few tens of mV (assumed)
